FAST

BERLIN, Nov 15 : FIFA president Gianni Infantino should be replaced as he has made world football's governing body worse than it was under disgraced former chief Sepp Blatter, Germany coach Juergen Klopp said on Sunday. Speaking a day before Germany's Nations League game against the Netherlands, Klopp said the situation at FIFA was potentially worse than under Blatter, who stepped down amid a corruption scandal and later faced criminal charges. "The opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense," Klopp told a press conference. "I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone managed to do just that." Infantino, also Swiss, was elected FIFA president in 2016 after a corruption scandal brought Blatter's tenure to an end. Blatter was later acquitted in a Swiss criminal case concerning a two-million-Swiss-franc payment to former UEFA president Michel Platini.

"At the moment we think that if Infantino goes that then the next one could maybe do it better. I think it is possible to make it better," Klopp said. "There are certainly people out there who care about the future of football and have no financial interest linked to that, and if they come together and one of them would become president, it would be helpful." Infantino, who is up for re-election in March 2027 and who has vowed to stay on, came under heavy criticism in July after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions, including the World Cup.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Una nueva historia del teléfono tiene una lección para la inteligencia artificial
item.description: La historia del teléfono, desde su invención hasta la transformación de las comunicaciones, ofrece algunas pistas sobre cómo la inteligencia artificial podría cambiar la sociedad. Un libro de James Gl ...
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brustein
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — En 1911, treinta y cinco años después de la invención del teléfono, Gerald Stanley Lee, un exministro convertido en ensayista sobre tecnología, se maravilló ante las implicaciones de estos aparatos. “No solo estamos inventando nuevas máquinas, sino que estas se han vuelto contra nosotros y están creando nuevos hombres”, escribió. “El teléfono cambia la estructura del cerebro. Los hombres viven en mayores distancias, piensan en términos más amplios y se vuelven receptivos a motivaciones más nobles y de mayor alcance”. Se puede discrepar de la afirmación de que nuestros motivos se han vuelto más nobles, pero es difícil negar que los teléfonos lo cambiaron todo. La cita de Lee aparece como epígrafe en una parte de El teléfono: una nueva historia , de James Gleick , un libro que entrelaza la ciencia, la economía y la cultura de los teléfonos para desarrollar la misma idea con mayor profundidad. Ver más: La tecnología del siglo XIX que Nvidia quiere cambiar para impulsar los centros de datos de IA Como argumenta convincentemente Gleick, las nuevas tecnologías importantes surgen sin forma definida; luego, la forma en que las personas las utilizan las moldea, influyendo a su vez en sus usuarios. Nadie puede observar el proceso en tiempo real, y desde luego nadie puede controlarlo. Para un libro cuya acción transcurre principalmente entre las décadas de 1870 y 1980, resulta sorprendentemente relevante para nuestra actual era de efervescencia tecnológica. En sus libros anteriores, Gleick demostró su habilidad para explicar conceptos complejos como la teoría del caos, la teoría de la información y la ciencia de los viajes en el tiempo. El libro El teléfono comienza recorriendo la historia de la telefonía a través de las vivencias de un puñado de inventores que la impulsaron. Esto desemboca en una carrera entre dos hombres en la década de 1870. Por un lado, Alexander Graham Bell, quien, por poseer la patente original, suele ser considerado el inventor del teléfono (el imperio empresarial que construyó a su alrededor se convirtió en el monopolio que definió el primer siglo de la telefonía). Pero también estaba Elisha Gray, quien, según Gleick, merece mayor reconocimiento. El día de San Valentín de 1876, ambos presentaron solicitudes de patente relacionadas con el teléfono ante la oficina de patentes. Los adinerados mecenas de Bell, escribe Gleick, se adelantaron y contactaron primero con un funcionario de patentes corrupto y ebrio, asegurándose así una de las propiedades intelectuales más valiosas de la historia. Gray no lo consiguió y, con razón, guardó rencor durante el resto de su vida. Sin embargo, no quedó claro de inmediato para qué serviría el teléfono. Sus primeros defensores pensaron que funcionaría principalmente como un medio de distribución masiva para actuaciones musicales, sermones religiosos y propaganda gubernamental. Otros menospreciaron la importancia de una herramienta que, como dijo Thomas Edison, no servía para nada más que para “conversaciones triviales”. También estaban los agoreros de los teléfonos. Edwin Butler, editor del Stark County News de Toulon, Illinois , predijo que estos dispositivos volverían a la gente más perezosa, socavarían la privacidad y “multiplicarían un millón de veces el poder de la conversación humana, inundando el mundo con charlas”. Butler prosiguió diciendo que, con el tiempo, todos tendrían teléfonos junto a la cama, agotando sus nervios al consumir noticias y chismes las veinticuatro horas del día. Hoy en día, esta preocupación resulta a la vez pintoresca y profética. Las costumbres sociales iban y venían. Gleick escribe de forma amena sobre las relaciones parasociales que la gente establecía con las operadoras telefónicas, en su mayoría mujeres, elegidas por su habilidad para hablar con dulzura a quienes llamaban. También aprovecha para divertir al máximo el material educativo de AT&T, que explicaba cosas tan básicas como cuánto tiempo dejar sonar un teléfono antes de colgar (de ocho a diez veces) y qué decir al contestar un teléfono que suena (“Hola. Residencia Matthews. Soy Jimmy”). Un folleto incluso ofrecía una lista ilustrada con sugerencias de personas a las que se podía llamar, como tenderos y médicos. Según Gleick, tales instrucciones rudimentarias no eran necesarias. Los teléfonos eran intuitivos y la gente creaba normas simplemente llamándose entre sí. Otros ejercían influencia sin necesidad de llamar directamente a nadie. Como señala un jurista, “fueron los abogados, tanto como cualquier otro, quienes inventaron el teléfono”. La patente original de Bell dio origen al monopolio del Sistema Bell, mediante el cual la American Telephone & Telegraph Company decidía qué funcionaría mejor para sus fines. Su departamento legal obligaba entonces a todos los demás a acatar esas decisiones, incluso en lo que respecta al diseño de los teléfonos en los hogares. A pesar de este férreo control, la innovación fue constante. Gleick presenta la era del teléfono como la prehistoria de internet, especialmente al describir cómo los avances en la conmutación telefónica sentaron las bases para los transistores que impulsarían las computadoras y sus redes. Mientras tanto, los usuarios de teléfonos desarrollaron el gusto por las conversaciones informales propias de la era telefónica, que con el tiempo se convertirían en la inteligencia colectiva de la World Wide Web. Aunque en la portada de El teléfono aparece un teléfono inteligente, el libro solo menciona la era del iPhone de pasada. La historia de Gleick concluye el 1 de enero de 1984, día en que décadas de litigios antimonopolio alcanzaron a AT&T y se disolvió el monopolio del sistema Bell. Gleick cierra su relato de forma concisa al señalar que este cambio trascendental en el sector de la telefonía se produjo exactamente un año después de que la red Arpanet del gobierno estadounidense adoptara el estándar de comunicaciones que hizo posible el internet moderno. Estos cambios tecnológicos y legales sentaron las bases para el lanzamiento del iPhone y todo lo que conllevó. Gleick no se detiene mucho en la afirmación de Lee de que los teléfonos han reorganizado nuestros cerebros. Pero escribe: “Ahora es difícil para cualquiera sentir lo que significaba para toda la humanidad estar desconectada, por defecto, no por un circuito roto ocasional o una línea muerta, sino como un hecho de la vida”. Podría decirse que es igualmente difícil para quienes solo han vivido en la era de los teléfonos inteligentes comprender la vida anterior, cuando la persona promedio sabía leer un mapa de papel y quizás echaba un vistazo a un periódico impreso con regularidad. Y, menos de cuatro años después de la introducción de ChatGPT, parece que estamos en las primeras etapas de otro cambio tecnológico monumental. Entre quienes desarrollan la IA existen desacuerdos fundamentales sobre la naturaleza misma de esta tecnología: ¿Es una mente alienígena? ¿Es realmente un potente software de productividad? Las normas culturales sobre su uso apenas comienzan a surgir, con dificultad. Y quienes deberían estar a cargo de desarrollar un marco legal para ella no han demostrado estar a la altura del desafío. Al describir el mundo que creó el teléfono, Gleick escribe que es un mundo que Bell “jamás habría imaginado y que no le habría gustado”. Es muy probable que, si dentro de cien años se siguen escribiendo libros, se pueda decir lo mismo de la IA. Pero, como ilustra El teléfono , los inventores no tienen la última palabra. Ver más: Analistas recortan previsiones de ganancias del S&P 500 para 2027 ante dudas sobre el gasto en IA

FAST

LONDON, Nov 15 : London City Lionesses tightened their grip on third place in the Women's Super League after goalkeeper Mary Earps produced a string of superb saves, including a stunning late intervention, to secure a 1-1 draw at Arsenal on Sunday. Earps finished with eight saves in her third start for Lionesses, preserving a valuable point in the closing stages when Frida Maanum lofted an audacious effort towards the top corner, only for the former England goalkeeper to get the slightest touch on the ball and divert it onto the crossbar. The visitors had fought back from an early setback through Isobel Goodwin, whose equaliser came barely a minute after Maanum had given Arsenal the lead in the 10th minute with a composed finish from Alessia Russo's cutback. Arsenal, who have yet to win a league game at home this season, looked set to take control at the Emirates Stadium when Russo burst into the area and pulled the ball back for Maanum to sweep into the bottom corner.

But London City responded immediately as Goodwin broke free of Leah Williamson and rifled a powerful finish high into the net to silence the home crowd. "It's obviously a big point away from home," Earps told Sky Sports. "I thought either team probably could have won it in terms of chances, a lot of counter-attacking. "But really happy that we got the point. Would have liked three, so we'll go back to the training ground and work out how we could have made that difference to get the three points." Arsenal pressed for a winner after the break, but Earps repeatedly frustrated the hosts and capped her display with the dramatic late save from Maanum's looping effort. The eight saves were her most in a WSL game since 2017. The result kept London City third on 20 points, six behind leaders Chelsea, while Arsenal remained sixth on 14 points. "It all becomes one big blur, and you're sort of hoping the ref's going to blow the whistle," said Earps, who joined London City in the close season after two years at Paris St Germain. "But all the girls put their body on the line, and obviously I love defending the goal, I love making saves. So anything I can do to help the team and use that energy from a save to gain us some momentum." Earlier on Sunday, Mathilde Harviken struck in the 76th minute to earn Aston Villa a 1-0 win over Birmingham City, leaving Villa seventh and Birmingham 13th. Viviane Asseyi scored either side of halftime as West Ham United beat bottom side Charlton Athletic 2-0. West Ham climbed to ninth, while Charlton remained without a point after 10 league matches.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Carney y Lula estrechan lazos con inversión de US$392 millones para proteger bosques tropicales
item.description: El primer ministro Mark Carney anunció una contribución de hasta US$392 millones durante cuatro años al mecanismo impulsado por Brasil y Noruega, que busca proteger más de 1.000 millones de hectáreas ...
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El primer ministro de Canadá, Mark Carney, y el presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dieron a conocer el domingo su intención de estrechar lazos mediante la financiación destinada a proteger los bosques tropicales del mundo y el intercambio de visitas a sus respectivos países. Ambos líderes se reunieron el domingo al margen de la cumbre de la Asociación de Naciones del Sudeste Asiático (ASEAN) celebrada en Manila. Carney anunció una financiación de hasta 560 millones de dólares canadienses (US$392 millones) a lo largo de cuatro años para un proyecto de financiación global en favor de los bosques liderado por Brasil. Ver más: ONU reclama nuevas medidas climáticas ante el fracaso para contener el calentamiento global Lula declaró a los periodistas en Manila que había invitado a Carney a Brasil durante los tres primeros meses del próximo año y que él visitaría Canadá en el segundo trimestre. Canadá es un país “con el que queremos reforzar nuestras relaciones para poder duplicar nuestro comercio”, afirmó Lula, reelegido como presidente de la mayor economía latinoamericana el pasado noviembre. Carney y Lula han aunado esfuerzos con la Unión Europea y Kenia en una iniciativa denominada Partners for Multilateralism (P4M), destinada a fomentar la cooperación mundial, con el objetivo de contrarrestar la diplomacia transaccional del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Lula afirmó el domingo, en un discurso dirigido a los líderes de la ASEAN, que reforzar la cooperación era la “mayor necesidad de nuestro tiempo” y resultaba imprescindible para el desarrollo sostenible y la reducción de la desigualdad. Más tarde, en declaraciones a la prensa, señaló que la estrategia de Brasil ante los aranceles de Trump consistía en “en lugar de lamentarse o suplicar al Gobierno de Estados Unidos”, salvaguardar su posición mediante la diversificación de sus socios comerciales. La financiación anunciada por Carney representa la contribución inicial de Canadá al Tropical Forest Forever Facility , un mecanismo de financiación liderado por Brasil y Noruega. Una vez que esté plenamente operativo, el proyecto protegerá más de 1.000 millones de hectáreas de bosques tropicales al año en más de 70 países. Ver más: El Niño sumará hasta 0,2°C a las temperaturas globales y prolongará el calor extremo hasta 2027 La contribución forma parte del objetivo de Canadá de proporcionar 13.000 millones de dólares canadienses en ayuda relacionada con el clima a los países en desarrollo de aquí a 2031, según indicó la oficina de Carney en un comunicado. FAST

Nov 15 : Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho played his first competitive match in 11 years at the age of 46, starting for Italian third-tier side Ravenna in their derby against Forli on Sunday. Wearing the number 10 shirt, Ronaldinho played the entire first half. At the interval, he took a lap of the pitch at the Stadio Bruno Benelli, waving to supporters as they stood to applaud him. Ravenna beat Forli 2-0 in the Serie C clash. Ronaldinho played a part in Giulio Donati's 36th-minute opener and Simone Rabbi added the second in the 58th. “It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sport Italia. He said he had enjoyed playing alongside team mates who had grown up watching him.

Ronaldinho had last played professionally for Fluminense in September 2015 and formally retired in 2018. Ravenna, whose president Ignazio Cipriani is a long-time friend of the Brazilian, announced his signing in June, with Ronaldinho also taking a stake in the club. The former AC Milan forward won the World Cup with Brazil in 2002, the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and the Champions League with Barcelona in 2006. "It went by too fast, that has always been football for me," he said. Asked whether he might make another appearance for Ravenna, Ronaldinho said: "Now if the President calls me, I’ll be back."

item.description: Nov 15 : Russia will miss the 2027 World Junior Championship because of entry restrictions imposed by the Canadian government, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed on Sunday.The IIHF said it had considered alternative arrangements but decided Canada would remain as host, with the tournamen
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Ice hockey-Russia to miss World Juniors over Canada restrictions, IIHF confirms

The logo of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) is seen in front of its seat in Zurich, Switzerland April 26, 2016. REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann

16 Nov 2026 02:37AM (Updated: 16 Nov 2026 04:05AM)

FAST

Nov 15 : Russia will miss the 2027 World Junior Championship because of entry restrictions imposed by the Canadian government, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed on Sunday. The IIHF said it had considered alternative arrangements but decided Canada would remain as host, with the tournament proceeding from December 26 to January 5 in Edmonton and Red Deer. Citing Russia's war in Ukraine, Canada's Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden told Reuters on Wednesday that Canada would deny entry to Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials coming to compete, even those with valid visas. The IIHF suspended teams from both countries in 2022 after Moscow launched its invasion from Russian and Belarusian territory, although last month’s Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordered the federation to readmit Russian teams to five championships.

The World Juniors were the first of the five tournaments covered by the October 30 ruling. The IIHF said it disagreed with the ruling but would comply. Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said Canada would not permit Russian athletes to compete for their country on Canadian soil, a statement some perceived as keeping the door open for their participation as neutrals. Van Koeverden said Canada allowed neutral participation only by individual athletes, ruling out that option for the Russian team. The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee to resolve the situation. "The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it said in a statement. "The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments." NORWAY BACK  The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said its under-20 team had been reinstated after previously being told it would have to make way for Russia as the lowest-ranked side in the tournament. "We’re very happy for the players, the coaches and everyone in Norwegian ice hockey, who earned this place by winning promotion last year," association secretary general Petter Salsten said. “The team have been looking forward to this for a whole year but have spent the past month in limbo.” Norway said its pre-tournament training camp and games in Canada would go ahead as planned. Russia's potential return to international ice hockey has prompted boycott threats ahead of next year's men's World Championship in Germany. Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden have said they would refuse to face Russia. One sponsor has withdrawn, while others have said they could follow if Russia take part. The German Ice Hockey Federation urged the IIHF to provide clarity over the men's World Championship. "We now need this planning security for our home World Championship in May, for the teams, the fans and all partners," federation chairman Frank Lutz said in a statement. "We therefore demand prompt clarification from the IIHF." Russian President Vladimir Putin said earlier this month that countries opposing rulings allowing Russia to return to international sport were violating the rights of Russian athletes and democratic institutions.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 15 : England starters Seb Atkinson, Ollie Chessum and George Furbank have all been cleared to train again ahead of next Saturday's Nations Championship clash against New Zealand. The trio were injured in the 45–22 victory over Australia at the start of the month's programme and missed Saturday's 78-15 victory over Japan, England's record score in the fixture. Uncapped Harlequins flanker Jack Kenningham has also been called up to a 36-man squad in place of the injured Tom Curry, the Rugby Football Union said on Sunday. A win over New Zealand would give England a chance of finishing top of the Northern Hemisphere section and taking a place in the November 29 final of the inaugural competition.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

item.title: El envejecimiento de los ‘baby boomers’, un factor que impulsa al mercado de bonos corporativos
item.description: Los inversores particulares han destinado US$268.000 millones a fondos de bonos estadounidenses de alta calidad hasta septiembre, casi el doble que en 2025. Los rendimientos cercanos al 6% y la búsque ...
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Los ciudadanos estadounidenses de a pie que buscan asegurarse unos ingresos relativamente elevados se han convertido este año, de forma sorprendente, en grandes compradores de bonos corporativos estadounidenses, lo que los ha convertido en una importante fuente de demanda de estos valores, a pesar de que los rendimientos se han disparado en los últimos meses. Los inversores particulares han invertido US$268.000 millones en fondos de bonos estadounidenses de alta calidad vinculados a un índice agregado hasta septiembre de este año, casi el doble de la cantidad registrada en el mismo periodo de 2025, según escribieron el mes pasado estrategas de Barclays Plc, entre ellos Dominique Toublan. Ver más: Analistas recortan previsiones de ganancias del S&P 500 para 2027 ante dudas sobre el gasto en IA Los bonos corporativos representan aproximadamente una cuarta parte de las tenencias de estos fondos, lo que significa que gran parte de ese dinero se canaliza hacia los mercados de deuda corporativa. En parte debido a esas compras, los inversores particulares poseen ahora alrededor del 17% del mercado de bonos corporativos de alta calificación y de alto rendimiento, el porcentaje más alto desde principios de 2022, justo cuando la Reserva Federal comenzó a subir los tipos de interés. La última afluencia de inversores particulares rompe con las tendencias históricas: los inversores particulares suelen reducir sus carteras cuando la rentabilidad se vuelve negativa, lo que aumenta la presión vendedora en épocas de crisis. Sin embargo, este año han intervenido precisamente cuando los rendimientos han ido en aumento. La demanda no suele ser suficiente para impulsar los precios, pero ha contribuido a frenar las ventas masivas y a mantener los diferenciales de los bonos corporativos relativamente ajustados. Las primas de riesgo de los bonos estadounidenses de alta calificación se han ampliado solo 0,1 puntos porcentuales este año, hasta situarse, al cierre del martes, en 0,88 puntos porcentuales. A pesar de esa ampliación, los diferenciales son mucho más estrechos que la media de 1,09 puntos porcentuales registrada durante la última década. Probablemente, la demanda proviene de inversores, entre ellos jubilados, que buscan obtener rendimientos relativamente elevados durante años, según Bradford Smith, gestor de carteras de renta fija en Janus Henderson Investors. Tras las caídas de los precios de los bonos registradas este año, los compradores tienen ahora acceso a deuda de primera categoría que ofrece elevados ingresos. Por ejemplo, los bonos a 30 años de Microsoft ( MSFT ), vendidos a finales de octubre y que cuentan con una calificación crediticia superior a la del Gobierno de EE.UU., ofrecen un rendimiento superior al 6%. El rendimiento medio de un bono corporativo estadounidense al cierre del martes se situaba en torno al 5,9%. “Para quienes viven de ingresos fijos o se financian con sus ahorros para la jubilación, estos niveles resultan especialmente atractivos”, afirmó Smith. Esta oportunidad resulta especialmente atractiva para los “baby boomers” que buscan alejarse de la volatilidad de la renta variable y obtener ingresos estables al jubilarse. Las personas mayores de 65 años representan un 18 % de la población estadounidense, una cifra récord, según datos de la Reserva Federal de San Luis. “Da la sensación de que el sector minorista está aceptando por fin el contexto de los tipos de interés”, afirmó Stephanie Doyle, gestora de carteras de renta fija de JPMorgan Asset Management, en una entrevista. Los hogares han invertido cada vez más en el mercado a través de soluciones de jubilación basadas en un único fondo, como los fondos con fecha objetivo, señaló Daniel Sorid, responsable de estrategia de crédito con calificación de inversión en EE.UU. en Citigroup ( C ). Estos instrumentos reajustan la asignación entre acciones y bonos y adoptan un mayor peso en renta fija a medida que los clientes envejecen, una medida destinada a proteger su patrimonio frente a la volatilidad. Sin embargo, las expectativas del mercado de al menos tres subidas más de un cuarto de punto en los tipos de interés estadounidenses de aquí a finales de 2027 suponen un riesgo para el impulso reciente. Los inversores minoristas ansían rendimientos jugosos, pero la posibilidad de que bajen los precios de sus inversiones amenaza con mermar su rentabilidad total. “Aunque a los inversores particulares les gustan los rendimientos más elevados, quieren que estos se mantengan estables”, afirmó Hans Mikkelsen, estratega de crédito de TD Securities. No obstante, las subidas de tipos podrían causar aún más daño a las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial que cotizan con valoraciones elevadas, lo que convertiría a los bonos corporativos de alta calificación en un refugio relativamente seguro, según Smith, de Janus Henderson. Para los jubilados, esta clase de activos ofrece el doble beneficio de la preservación del capital y unos ingresos fiables con los que vivir. Rara vez en la historia reciente han generado los bonos corporativos unos rendimientos tan elevados, y ello ocurrió en su mayor parte en momentos de crisis, como la crisis financiera mundial de 2008. Ver más: El dólar cierra su mejor semana en más de un mes ante apuestas por un alza de tasas de la Fed “Se están observando rendimientos absolutos en títulos a largo plazo de Meta, o de empresas muy conocidas, que los inversores particulares están empezando a considerar realmente atractivos”, afirmó Annie Seelaus, directora ejecutiva de R. Seelaus & Co., en el podcast “Credit Edge” de Bloomberg Intelligence el mes pasado. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Nvidia row: Lutnick pushed to weaken chip rules linked to family business
item.description: Cantor Fitzgerald has financial ties to Southeast Asian data centre firms serving Chinese clients as US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick weighs tighter curbs on advanced AI chip sales ...
item.dc:creator: NYT
item.content:encoded: By Ana Swanson, Aaron Krolik & Paul Mozur In Malaysia’s lush southern peninsula, a data center known as A201 is set to open next year, packed with hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) servers. The data center plans to supply this computing power to a Chinese tech giant. The setup is legal and profitable. It will also sidestep United States (US) rules that ban sales of the most advanced AI chips directly to Chinese firms. The firm operating the data centre is a client of Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm formerly led by Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, who handed off leadership of it to his sons. Lutnick is now writing the rules that would have a substantial effect on the data center’s business. Lutnick has been seen as a force slowing rules that would clamp down on the sale of Nvidia chips to data centers like A201, which sit outside China but provide AI computing power to Chinese firms. The Trump administration, concerned about ceding the country’s advantage in AI, bans the sale of cutting-edge chips to China. But it has been embroiled in an internal debate for much of the past two years over how far to go in limiting chip sales to data centers in Southeast Asia. On one side of the debate are China hawks, who see the data centres as a way for Beijing to do an end run around the chip sales ban. On the other are officials, most prominently Lutnick, who are pushing against going too far in limiting the ability of US companies like Nvidia to sell their products in Asia. Recently, Lutnick has been advocating a less stringent version of those controls under consideration, which could cut back on Nvidia’s business by giving the US government more oversight of chip sales to international data centres.  Cantor Fitzgerald has had business dealings with several data centre firms in Southeast Asia that cater to Chinese clients, and could be affected by the regulations Lutnick is drafting, a review by The New York Times has found. Cantor Fitzgerald served as a designated sales agent for an equity offering of up to $1 billion this year by Bitdeer, the Singaporean firm that will operate data center A201, in addition to having other financial ties to various global data center businesses. The relationship between the two companies began as early as 2024, when Cantor Fitzgerald helped Bitdeer arrange a stock offering of up to $250 million. Lutnick steered Cantor Fitzgerald for decades, before recusing himself when he joined the Trump administration last year. The Commerce Department says Lutnick has complied with all ethics agreements, and his former business is now run by his sons. These dealings are just a tiny portion of Cantor’s business, which stretches from investment banking and trading to real estate. There is no evidence that Cantor’s investments influenced Lutnick’s deliberations. ‘Go outside the company’ to find new CEO: Bessent US Treasury  Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said Nvidia needs to “go outside the company” as it seeks a new chief executive officer (CEO) after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last weekafter revelations of extramarital affairs. Reuters

FAST

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 15 : Women's Tennis Association Chair Valerie Camillo said she expects a return to "normal operations, normal financials" in 2027 and that she has full confidence in its outlook despite reports the tour could run short of cash. The Telegraph reported in September that the WTA projects operating losses of $23 million this year, adding that its accounts could move into the red by autumn 2027. Camillo did not directly address the reported figures when asked in an interview with Reuters at the WTA Finals, but said that 2026 was a year of transition. More than a billion people watched women's tennis last year, leaving it well placed for growth, she said.

"Everyone should be very confident in the future of the WTA," she said. RELOCATION COSTS This year, the tour absorbed the unexpected cost of moving the season-ending event to Indian Wells, after deciding to end an agreement under which Riyadh hosted the Finals with the backing of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF). The WTA ended the three-year deal after two years to secure certainty over where the event would be held, given uncertainty in the region, she said. Camillo said the tour took on the full financial investment of staging the tournament and was also funding the Finals prize money pool in full. She described the PIF as a continuing partner, noting that it still sponsors the tour's maternity fund and is a sponsor of this year's Finals. Pressure on finances is also tied to CVC Capital Partners, which acquired a 20 per cent stake in the WTA's commercial arm in 2023 for $150 million paid over five years. That funding, about $30 million a year, ends in 2027. EQUAL PRIZE MONEY Asked about criticism that the CVC money had gone too heavily into prize money, Camillo said equal pay was the foundation of the tour and that prize money would not be cut. She said all combined WTA-ATP Masters 1000 events would offer equal prize money next year, joining the Grand Slams. The WTA has not yet set prize money for the 2027 Finals. In September, Camillo said the tour was considering alternatives including a profit-sharing model with players. This year's total prize pool of $10 million is a drop from $15.5 million in 2025. Camillo also described a new Tournament Investment Fund, designed to help tournaments keep strong player fields and to support events in weaker calendar slots. It is part of the 2027 calendar overhaul after players asked for lighter commitments. Under the changes, the number of WTA 500 events each player is committed to will fall from six to four. CHARLOTTE AND TOUR UNIFICATION The WTA will stage the Finals in Charlotte, North Carolina, for at least three years from 2027. The event will be indoors at the Spectrum Center, home of the NBA's Charlotte Hornets. That could shrink the Finals from their current eight-day run down to five days to accommodate the NBA's schedule. Camillo said a format is being developed with players and an announcement is expected soon. She also said talks continue on closer cooperation between the men's and women's tours, but said any deal must be right for the women's game and protect its marketing profile. Camillo also cited new initiatives such as a collaboration with TikTok and one with Mercedes-Benz, which will see the winner of Sunday's final driving away with an SL 55 in the WTA's signature purple color. "We continue our really strong commercial growth, attracting new partnerships, and we're now self-operating our Finals, our media rights, our production," she said. "Our future trajectory is incredible."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Analistas recortan previsiones de ganancias del S&P 500 para 2027 ante dudas sobre el gasto en IA
item.description: Las previsiones de crecimiento de las ganancias del índice cayeron durante cuatro semanas consecutivas y ahora apuntan a un avance del 20% en 2027, frente al 30% estimado para este año.
item.dc:creator: Chloé Meley
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Los analistas están revisando a la baja sus previsiones sobre los beneficios del S&P 500 para el próximo año, incluso cuando la temporada de resultados del tercer trimestre, que ha sido espectacular, llega a su fin, ya que las preocupaciones sobre el gasto en inteligencia artificial y las repercusiones de las elecciones de mitad de legislatura en Estados Unidos ensombrecen las perspectivas. Las previsiones para el índice de referencia se han revisado a la baja durante cuatro semanas consecutivas, y ahora se espera que los beneficios crezcan un 20% en 2027, según datos de Bloomberg Intelligence . Esta cifra está por debajo del crecimiento del 30% previsto para este año. Ver más: Startups brasileñas apuestan por la ‘IA física’ y encuentran en el agronegocio un motor de crecimiento Estos recortes se producen a pesar de que todos los sectores del S&P 500 han superado las expectativas previas a la temporada en cuanto a beneficios por acción, y ya se ha publicado más del 80% del valor de mercado del índice, según muestran los datos de BI. El crecimiento del beneficio por acción del índice alcanzó el 33%, ligeramente por encima del 32 % registrado en el segundo trimestre, impulsado por los gigantes de la energía y la tecnología. “Las tendencias generales de las previsiones son alentadoras, pero una victoria arrolladora de los demócratas aumenta el riesgo de retrasos en el gasto en IA, el principal motor del crecimiento del beneficio por acción del S&P 500 en los últimos tres años”, escribieron en una nota las estrategas del Bank of America ( BAC ) Savita Subramanian y Victoria Roloff, refiriéndose a los avances demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura. Las dudas sobre el futuro de la regulación de la IA y la política en materia de centros de datos se han sumado a los temores ya existentes respecto a un gasto descontrolado en computación para la IA, lo que ha alimentado una ola de ventas de acciones tecnológicas. Según Vivek Arya, analista de BofA, los analistas podrían recortar aún más las estimaciones de ganancias por acción (EPS) en el primer trimestre si los cambios en las políticas se traducen en recortes en el gasto de capital a partir del próximo año. Un recorte del 20% en el gasto de capital en IA podría reducir las ganancias por acción del S&P 500 hasta en un 8%, según un estudio de BofA. Los retrasos en la concesión de permisos, la oposición local a la construcción de centros de datos y la creciente cautela en torno a las empresas de neocloud (proveedores de infraestructura en la nube especializados y creados principalmente para impulsar la IA) podrían ralentizar el ritmo de los nuevos desarrollos, según ha señalado el analista de Citigroup ( C ), Atif Malik. Una expansión más lenta de los centros de datos tendría repercusiones tanto en las propias empresas de IA como en los fabricantes de equipos y los proveedores de energía , terrenos y mano de obra, según escribieron los estrategas de UBS, liderados por Keith Parker. Esto “reduce la fuerza del impulso favorable para el sector en expansión”. Fuera del sector de la IA, las perspectivas no son mucho más alentadoras, sobre todo para las empresas que tienen como objetivo principal al consumidor. Ver más: Mythos, la IA de Anthropic que busca fallos cibernéticos en los sistemas energéticos Según Subramanian y Roloff, de Bank of America, las previsiones de beneficios para las empresas de consumo se han mantenido “sorprendentemente bien” desde el inicio de la guerra con Irán. Sin embargo, el impulso derivado de la devolución de aranceles se ha desvanecido en gran medida y las revisiones de las previsiones del grupo para 2027 se han quedado rezagadas con respecto al mercado en general esta temporada. Esto deja a la inflación y los tipos de interés como los principales factores determinantes, afirmaron. Los resultados de Walmart ( WMT ) y Target ( TGT ) la próxima semana deberían mostrar cómo los consumidores están afrontando la inflación y cómo el sector de bienes de consumo básico está mitigando la presión, según los analistas de Business Insider, Wendy Soong y Christopher Cain. Nvidia ( NVDA ), que también presentará sus resultados la próxima semana, pondrá a prueba al sector de la IA. Para el fabricante de chips, “el riesgo clave no reside en la demanda de 2027, que parece estar en gran medida comprometida, sino en la visibilidad de los pedidos de 2028 y la conversión de la cartera de pedidos pendientes”, afirmó Malik, de Citi. item.title: Economía de Perú desacelera en septiembre y pone en riesgo su meta de crecimiento para 2026
item.description: La actividad económica peruana creció 2,43% interanual en septiembre, por debajo de todas las estimaciones de los analistas consultados por Bloomberg. La caída de la minería y la agricultura contrasta ...
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La economía de Perú se desaceleró de forma inesperada en septiembre, lastrada por la débil producción minera y agrícola. El índice de actividad económica, un indicador del producto interior bruto, aumentó un 2,43% con respecto al año anterior, según informó el domingo el Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Información (INEI). El resultado fue inferior al 3,32% revisado de agosto y por debajo de todas las estimaciones de los economistas encuestados por Bloomberg, así como de la estimación mediana del 3,5%. La producción aumentó un 0,09% respecto al mes anterior. Ver más: Por qué Chile dejaría de ser la cuarta economía de Sudamérica y podría ser superada por Perú en 2027 El crecimiento inferior al esperado en septiembre indica que Perú podría tener dificultades para alcanzar la previsión del banco central de un crecimiento del 3,2% para 2026, a pesar de la sólida inversión privada y los elevados precios de los metales. Se espera que estos factores favorables ayuden a amortiguar el impacto en la economía de un inminente y fuerte fenómeno meteorológico de El Niño, que ya está afectando negativamente a la agricultura, la pesca y las industrias relacionadas. En los primeros nueve meses de 2026, la actividad económica creció un 3,18%. En términos interanuales, el crecimiento de septiembre se vio impulsado por las ventas al por menor y la construcción, que registraron un aumento del 6,29% y del 8,84%, respectivamente. Por el contrario, la minería descendió un 6,32% en comparación con el año anterior debido a la menor producción de metales, mientras que la agricultura se redujo un 5,44 %. Perú figura desde hace tiempo entre las economías con mejor desempeño de América Latina, gracias a un crecimiento más rápido, una moneda estable y unos tipos de interés relativamente más bajos. La inflación también se había mantenido generalmente por debajo de la de sus pares regionales hasta que un repunte la llevó a superar el límite del 3% del rango objetivo del banco central y, posteriormente, a mantenerse por encima de este durante los últimos ocho meses, en un contexto donde el aumento de los precios de los alimentos se suma a la crisis energética mundial. A principios de esta semana, los responsables de la política monetaria elevaron los costos de endeudamiento en un cuarto de punto, hasta el 4,50% , por primera vez en casi cuatro años. La junta afirmó que su decisión no implica necesariamente el inicio de un ciclo de endurecimiento monetario, y añadió que ajustará la política según sea necesario para que la inflación vuelva a situarse dentro del rango objetivo. El 9 de noviembre, Perú recurrió a los mercados internacionales de bonos por primera vez en más de un año. El país, rico en cobre, vendió nuevos bonos por valor de US$4.500 millones en una operación dividida en dos partes y lanzó una oferta de canje de deuda, ofreciendo a los tenedores la opción de canjear bonos con vencimiento en 2027, 2030 y 2031 por nuevos bonos con vencimiento en 2038. Ver más: ¿En qué invertir en Chile, Perú y Colombia? Estas son las apuestas de este banco de inversión A finales de octubre, la administración de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori anunció que planea un gasto adicional de hasta 18.000 millones de soles (US$5.300 millones) para 2027, mediante la modificación de las reglas fiscales del Perú y la autorización de un déficit que aumente al 2,4% del producto interno bruto el próximo año, por encima del 1,4% anterior. Esto brindará a las autoridades mayor margen de maniobra para proteger la economía de las inclemencias del tiempo y del aumento de los precios mundiales del combustible. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

FAST

EDINBURGH, Nov 15 : Scotland held on for a narrow 15-12 win over Australia in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday, deepening the gloom for next year's World Cup hosts. Both sides scored two tries in an attritional and error-ridden battle that featured few moments of quality and a scoreless spell lasting more than 45 minutes. Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey went over for Scotland in the opening 27 minutes and Finn Russell added a conversion for a 12-5 halftime lead.  Russell's penalty stretched the advantage to 15-5 with six minutes remaining, before Max Jorgensen crossed in the final minute and Ben Donaldson converted. Australia had opened their account through winger Harry Potter's first-half try.

It was an eighth successive loss in Europe for the Wallabies, who showed early promise when new coach Les Kiss took over in August but now look devoid of confidence and in a rut. Australia had been heavily beaten by England at Twickenham a week earlier. Captain Harry Wilson said Sunday's performance represented a significant improvement, but the losing run leaves them under growing pressure with less than a year before their home World Cup kicks off on October 1. CAPTAIN MISSES OUT THROUGH INJURY Scotland overcame the overnight loss of captain Sione Tuipulotu to injury with his replacement Tom Jordan setting up the first try in the eighth minute. Scrumhalf Ben White's pass picked out Fagerson, who was alone on the touchline and went over to give Scotland the lead. Australia responded within three minutes after a sustained attack, flyhalf Carter Gordon delaying his pass before releasing Potter to score as Russell missed the tackle. Former Wallaby Dempsey finished off a pick and go, with Ewan Ashman and Fagerson driving towards the line and Dempsey carrying it over to put Scotland back ahead 12-5. There were no more points until the 74th minute when Australia were penalised for not clearing away at the ruck and Russell tucked over the penalty for a 10-point lead. But Australia then suddenly burst into life and threatened to set up a dramatic comeback as Jorgensen finished off some slick handling with less than a minute left on the clock. There was still time for Australia to collect the kick-off from Scotland and look for a winning try. They found some room on the left wing to threaten another score before being bundled into touch to end the contest. “It was a bit of an arm wrestle. Conditions played a part in that. It was a battle of the defences,” said Rory Darge, who captained the Scots in place of Tuipulotu. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

Source: Reuters

Nov 15 (Reuters) – Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its foreign minister said on Sunday, following a suspected sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on Moscow.

Estonian authorities detained eight people overnight on suspicion of an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems that they said had been ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service.

There was no immediate comment from Moscow on Estonia’s accusations or its decision to shut the border crossings. Moscow has regularly denied accusations by European authorities of involvement in sabotage operations.

Show Full Article

“Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences,” Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said in a post on X.

He did not specify how long the border closure would last or if an end date had been set.

Estonia, a NATO and European Union member state and a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has three open border crossings with Russia at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, which admit pedestrians and freight, according to Estonian public broadcaster ERR.

(Reporting by Andrius Sytas in Vilnius, Writing by Terje Solsvik, Editing by Louise Heavens and Gareth Jones)

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 15 : US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said Nvidia needs to "go outside the company" as it seeks a new chief executive after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis. "This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" show. Bessent also said Nvidia's board and outside counsel needed to answer, within the next 10 days, questions about the company's culture of compliance with export restrictions. Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential replacement for Huang, the Financial Times said on Friday.

Source: Reuters

FAST

TURIN, Nov 15 : World number one Alexander Zverev eased past debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets on Sunday to score an opening group win at the start of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German, a two-time champion at the season-ending tournament of the top eight players, bagged a break in each set to clinch a 6-4 6-4 victory over the 20-year-old Spaniard, who has played a sensational first season on tour and has risen from the mid-100s to the top 10 in less than 12 months. Jodar, however, could do little to tame Zverev's booming serve and the most experienced ATP Finals player in the field, playing his 31st match, earned a break to go 4-3 up with a superb backhand down the line. The Spaniard had two rare break chances at 5-4 behind but could not convert either. Instead Zverev bagged the set in the next game and grabbed a break early in the second set to open up a 3-1 lead.

FAST

Nov 15 : Rory McIlroy secured a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday, matching Colin Montgomerie's mark for the most Order of Merit victories in European Tour history before dedicating the achievement to his recovering father. The 37-year-old Northern Irishman carded a bogey-free 67 to seal a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai crown, edging Spain's Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings. Englishman Tyrrell Hatton, meanwhile, cruised to a five-shot victory at the DP World Tour Championship. The latest crown capped another fine year for McIlroy, who successfully defended his Masters title at Augusta National in April to secure a second green jacket and further cement his place among the game's greats.

"I don't really know what to say. Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," McIlroy told Sky Sports. "I remember Monty (Montgomerie) being a stalwart of the European Tour. Going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years, I remember playing with him for the first time at the London Club on the European Tour in 2008. "To pull up alongside him and win eight of these things, it means the world to me. "I'm a proud European. I'm a proud European player and I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour and I'm very proud of myself right now." The milestone carried added emotional significance for McIlroy, whose father has spent the past two months recovering from major surgery. "He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said. "But when I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went. He said to me: 'Go win the Race to Dubai.'"

Source: Reuters

FAST

BARCELONA, Nov 15 : Spanish second division team Tenerife returned to action on Sunday for the first time since the death of striker Jesus De Miguel, with emotional tributes before and during their game against Ceuta. De Miguel died on November 3, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a league match at home. Tributes took place around the country and on Sunday at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, Tenerife paid their own respects. A lengthy standing ovation bookended a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a further round of applause followed, while a video of De Miguel was shown around the stadium, as occurred in all first and second tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans also unfurled a banner reading "Jesus De Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white." Tenerife forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring in the 40th minute and he celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt to the crowd. Gil then revealed a message written under his shirt saying "Demi (De Miguel's nickname), always in our hearts." Neal Viereck added a second four minutes from time to seal a 2-0 win for Tenerife, ending a run of six games without a win. Tenerife are 14th in the Segunda standings, while Ceuta are bottom.  Last Saturday Tenerife's game with Granada was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. The squad and staff were present at the Heliodoro and in Navahermosa three days earlier, where De Miguel was laid to rest.

Source: Reuters

FAST

BUCHAREST: Drones have struck three commercial ships in the Black Sea near Romania's Sulina canal, Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said on Sunday (Nov 15), adding that his armed forces had scrambled fighter jets twice. Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea said there were no casualties and that the ships' crews had managed to control the fires on board after the strikes late on Saturday. A growing series of deadly strikes on merchant ships near NATO members Romania and Bulgaria shows how the escalating maritime war between Russia and Ukraine is expanding into a major challenge for the transatlantic alliance in the Black Sea. The Sulina canal is a key Romanian shipping lane which links the Danube river to the Black Sea and is used by Ukraine for exports.

Romanian officials did not identify the origin of the drones but said they were a direct consequence of Russia's war in Ukraine. "These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law," Niculescu said. "They reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine." Russia has denied targeting Ukraine's neighbours with drones. Oprea said the three struck ships were Greek-flagged oil and chemical tanker Evia Petrol V, bulk carrier Marsol and oil products tanker Ali Najafov, both under the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Evia Petrol V and Marsol were struck 4 and 5 nautical miles southeast of the Sulina canal, the defence ministry said, inside Romanian territorial waters. Oprea said a separate general cargo ship was hit by a drone late on Friday, also with no casualties. Private television station Digi24 said the vessel was Palau-flagged general cargo ship Larissa 1. "On Tuesday and Wednesday I will be in Brussels for the meeting with my fellow (defence) ministers," Oprea said. "We need the solidarity of our allies, shown through patrols with surveillance aircraft and through equipment for counter-drone warfare." France temporarily relocated the Atlantique 2 maritime patrols aircraft to Romania after it asked for reinforcement. Many of the ships hit in October and November were anchored near or sailing to or from the Sulina canal.

By Mikhail Flores and Nestor Corrales MANILA, Nov 15 (Reuters) – ASEAN and China were unable to conclude negotiations on a long-delayed South China Sea code of conduct under the Philippines’ chairmanship, despite reaching provisional agreement on about 80% of the draft, Manila’s foreign minister said on Sunday.

Negotiations on an ASEAN-China Code of Conduct in the South China Sea have dragged on for over two decades, but the Philippines, as current chair, had committed to speed up those talks and conclude the code this year.

“There is no conclusion yet,” Philippine foreign minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro told a press conference at a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila, adding that several key issues remain unresolved, including questions over whether the code would be legally binding.

Show Full Article

“The ASEAN countries plus China have also different views on how things are,” she added.

China’s Southeast Asian neighbours want the code to be grounded in international law, which they have repeatedly accused Beijing of disregarding as it asserts its sovereignty over nearly all of the South China Sea.

Beijing maintains that its actions in the South China Sea have been lawful and professional.

OVERLAPPING MARITIME CLAIMS

China’s extensive maritime claims overlap with the exclusive economic zones of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, making a functional code essential to preventing any escalation of tensions and managing incidents at sea.

An international arbitration tribunal ruled in 2016 that China’s sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision that Beijing rejects.

Manila and Beijing have been locked in a series of maritime confrontations in recent years, with the Philippines accusing China of repeated aggressive actions inside its exclusive economic zone, including dangerous manoeuvres, water‑cannoning and disrupting resupply missions.

China, for its part, has accused the Philippines of intruding into what it claims as its territory.

Analysts say the disagreements are not only between ASEAN and China.

Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, said divisions among ASEAN members, including over the geographical scope of the code, had also slowed negotiations.

“Other than Beijing, intramural divergences within ASEAN also play a significant role,” he said.

Koh said the remaining differences would be difficult to resolve and would require “major concessions” from the various parties.

Singapore will inherit the task of trying to secure agreement on the code of conduct when it assumes the ASEAN chairmanship next year.

(Writing by Karen Lema, editing by Gareth Jones)

By Michael Kahn PRAGUE, Nov 15 (Reuters) – Tens of thousands of Czechs protested in Prague on Sunday against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget – a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters’ independence and viability.

Opposition parties compared the proposals in an October bill to changes in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, who built an array of pro-government media.

Local authorities had estimated hundreds of thousands would attend the rally days before the November 17 holiday commemorating the 1989 Velvet Revolution that swept away Communist rule and propelled dissident playwright Vaclav Havel to power.

Show Full Article

The front section near the stage in Letna park overlooking the Czech capital filled quickly as protesters clogged nearby metro stations. Many wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers as tribute to an animated character who has introduced Czech Television’s nightly children’s bedtime stories for decades.

The populist government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis, backed by the far-right SPD and eurosceptic Motorists parties, accuses private and public media of bias.

The coalition backs a bill that would cancel a 205-crown ($9.26) monthly household broadcasting fee currently used for funding. The bill has passed a preliminary vote and awaits further debate.

Czech public television and radio workers escalated the fight with a one-day strike earlier in November that led to broadcast curbs and protests backed by artists and students.

Critics say the funding shift to the budget would undercut the media’s relationship with paying viewers and make the sector susceptible to political pressure.

A 15% financing cut proposed as part of the change would bring television’s nominal budget to the level of 2008 and radio’s to 2005. Media say that is unworkable.

Babis says the government is merely meeting a promise to lighten the financial burden on people.

($1 = 22.1280 Czech crowns)

(Reporting by Michael Kahn, Editing by Andrew Cawthorne)

BEIJING/HONG KONG: Hong Kong property developer New World Development on Sunday (Nov 15) proposed a rights issue to raise about HK$24.9 billion (US$3.17 billion), a company filing showed. New World Development has been trying to cut debt, dispose of assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit conditions and a weak property market. The plan offers shareholders 11 rights shares for every existing share at HK$0.90 each, representing a 26.9 per cent discount to the theoretical ex-rights price of HK$1.23 per share. The subscription price also represents an 81.5 per cent discount to the last closing price.

Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises (CTFE), which owns about 45.3 per cent of the company, has committed to take up its full entitlement and fully underwrite the remaining shares. The maximum CTFE commitment is about HK$18.7 billion. A CTFE statement said it supports New World Development resuming dividend payments when its financial performance and liquidity permit. The company plans to use about 34 per cent of the proceeds to prepay 10 per cent of about HK$82 billion in bank loans and extend the maturity of the remaining 90 per cent by two years. It plans to use another third to repay debt, including senior notes and deferred distribution of its perpetual securities. After the rights issue, New World's net debt to total equity ratio will drop to 48.3 per cent from 68.3 per cent. The developer aims to reduce total debt by between HK$40 billion and HK$50 billion by the end of 2031 to HK$93 billion to HK$103 billion New World's shares will resume trading on Monday after being suspended on Friday pending the announcement.

By Mohammed Ghobari Nov 15 (Reuters) – Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that squeezed oil exports.

Sunday’s announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis’ drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Show Full Article

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider Middle East conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February.

“The Southern Armed Forces announce the implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate,” the main military force fighting for Yemen’s government in the south of the country said in a statement.

“This step is taken based on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats.”

There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government’s main international ally.

HOUTHI GAINS

Yemen’s decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait that controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country’s third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

They also made significant advances in the highland areas north of Aden, cutting off Taiz in early October and putting increased pressure on the disparate coalition of forces fighting for the internationally recognised government.

GOVERNMENT FORCES STILL TRYING TO PUSH HOUTHIS FROM COAST

Around Bab el-Mandeb the government forces have redeployed to al-Suqyah, just south of Dhubab and 150 km (95 miles) west of Aden, but are still trying to push the Houthis from coastal areas nearby, Yemeni military sources said.

In the highlands south of Taiz, the Houthis are positioned just outside the district of Tur al-Bahah in Lahj governorate, about 80 km (50 miles) from Aden.

The Houthi gains around Taiz, which has become the fiercest front of the civil war, undermined the government campaign around Bab el-Mandeb, the military sources said.

Fighting is still intensifying around the western region of Taiz, with humanitarian conditions worsening. The city, which hosts about half of the 300,000 people displaced across Yemen by the latest fighting, remains besieged. Aid supplies are unable to enter, and civilians are unable to leave.

The Houthis have meanwhile released 600 prisoners, the International Committee of the Red Cross said on Sunday.

(Reporting by Mohammed Ghobari; Additional reporting by Reyam Mukhashaf in Aden; Writing by Nayera Abdallah and Angus McDowall; Editing by William Mallard and Peter Graff)
